result:
I've amended the architecture documents for all eight wave-RG1 items, and each one now matches the merged code (`1e6a545` backend, `5474a66` frontend). The changes are uncommitted, as asked. The DG4 historical validator passed (exit 0) at the start (14:31 UTC) and at the end (14:39 UTC). The Prettier check over `docs/architecture` also exits 0. I didn't re-run the unit, integration or e2e suites; the amendments cite the implementers' tests by file and line.

I checked each handback claim against the code before writing it. Every change is dated 2026-10-23 and cites D-185, in the style of the existing amendments. No code, contract or test was touched.

| Item | What I wrote |
|---|---|
| ADR-0003 §Migrations (F-DG5-100) | A new "Migration order" section: the runner refuses a pending file whose id isn't above the highest applied id. It covers the exact error message, `mth-db status` reporting `ORDER` (exit 4), and the tests. |
| p5-work-split rule 16 | The eight P5 gaps (0066, 0067, 0073, 0077, 0078, 0079, 0083, 0084) are retired and never filled; a new id goes above the highest shipped id. Each range's "leaves its number unused" sentence is marked, and the `p4-work-split.md` note to fill unused numbers is marked superseded for P5 and later. |
| ADR-0007 readiness | `migrations: fail` also covers an out-of-order pending file. The contract's `ok`/`pending`/`fail` values are unchanged. |
| ADR-0046 (F-DG5-101) | The CSV line reference is corrected in place (`csv.ts:66–68` → `:71–73`), and the mechanism now reads: the formula-prefix decision is made once and the CSV writer follows it. A new amendment E5 states that long negative decimals are unprefixed. |
| ADR-0050 and the data dictionary (F-DG5-121) | Amendment D21: the roaming launch plan carries its Day-90 test (scheduled 2026-10-01, open, 0/6), which is in the record counts and checksum. The `day_ninety_test` row now names the demo seed (synthetic) as a writer. |
| ADR-0044 §7 (F-DG5-120) | Amendment B5 names the screens: the Dependencies page section "Critical dependency slips", the initiative page section, and the work-item text built from `messageParams`. It also says the roadmap still shows no slip. |
| ADR-0049 §1 (F-DG5-122) | Amendment N3: tables render as tables, a one-cell table as a wrapping callout, and previews and snippets show cell text. Storage stays verbatim. |
| ADR-0042 (F-DG5-140) | Amendment V5: launch is offered only to users holding `procedure.launch`. It's a UI hint; the server check is unchanged. |

Three points where I didn't follow the handbacks word for word:
- **ADR-0042 "§4":** in that ADR, §4 is the state machines, which didn't change; the launch permission sits in §9. V5's title names both, and its marker is on the §9 launch row.
- **ADR-0050 §4/§5:** these sections never contained the phrase "the launch plan with its template tasks"; that's a comment in the seed code. D21 adds the Day-90 test to §4 and says §5's coverage check is unchanged.
- **"Inbox" in ADR-0044 B5:** the frontend handback mentions an inbox, but I found no separate inbox screen. B5 names only the screens I could confirm: My Work and the personal dashboard's My Work sections.

**For integration:**
- The worktree already had some untracked files when I started (`.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.mcp.json`, `.idea`, `CLAUDE.local.md` and others). They aren't mine and shouldn't be integrated.
- The DG5 candidate ID needs recomputing after you merge, because the documentation changed.

The handback, with the full item → amendment → evidence (`file:line`) table, is at `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/T-DG5-ARCH-RG1-solution-architect.md`.
